gate_sentence: Against the real append-only ledger, POST /api/missions/:id/verdicts deterministically rejects an uncited kill, refuses a second concurrent build (WIP=1), and refuses advance->validated without a recorded probe - enforced in Postgres-writing handlers, not by model choice.
method_note: All steps are real human invocations against the running Hono service on :4111 (real Postgres nonprod ledger) and the real holo CLI. No wholesale test-suite invocation (D7). Runs used: RUN_ECHO=019f8d2d-2ef7-711b-bb40-df20ab9f27e4 (test.echo, completed, NO research.plan@1 probe) for steps 1 + 3a; RUN_PROBE=019f8d2f-c5d5-7b9d-94d0-abcdde0a2f17 (research, has a committed research.plan@1 probe from its plan stage) for step 3b; RUN_CYCLE=019f8d2e-00db-7eda-8ef3-51ee6cd81018 (research) for steps 4 + 5. Step 2 uses the research template for the concurrent second-build because its fleet plan stage keeps the row in 'running' ~1-3s (vs test.echo's ~3ms), giving the WIP=1 partial unique index a reliable collision window.

steps.text: POST /api/missions/:id/verdicts {kill, no-citation} - rejected deterministically by the handler.
steps.literal_cmd: curl -sS -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/api/missions/019f8d2d-2ef7-711b-bb40-df20ab9f27e4/verdicts -H 'Authorization: Bearer rn-gate-s23' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"verdict":"kill","rationale":"Stop now, without a citation.","requestKey":"gate-step1-uncited-kill"}'

steps.text: Start a second concurrent build on the same subject - refused (WIP=1).
steps.literal_cmd:
TS=$(date +%s); G="Sprint-23 WIP1 concurrent test.echo subject $TS"; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -sS -o /tmp/gate-s23-wip-$i.json -w "R${i}_HTTP=%{http_code}
" --max-time 30 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/api/missions -H 'Authorization: Bearer rn-gate-s23' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{"templateKey":"test.echo","goal":"$G","idempotencyKey":"wip-burst-$TS-$i","args":{"goal":"$G"}}" & done; wait; echo; OKN=0; WIPN=0; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do B=$(tr -d '
' </tmp/gate-s23-wip-$i.json); echo "R${i}=$B"; echo "$B" | grep -q '"ok": *true' && OKN=$((OKN+1)); echo "$B" | grep -q 'WIP_ONE_EXCEEDED' && WIPN=$((WIPN+1)); done; echo "OK_COUNT=$OKN WIP_COUNT=$WIPN"; if [ "$OKN" -ge 1 ] && [ "$WIPN" -ge 1 ]; then P1='STEP2_PROOF=ok'; P2='wip_body'; printf '%s+%s
' "$P1" "$P2"; else N1='NO_WIP'; N2='_IN_BURST'; printf '%s%s
' "$N1" "$N2"; exit 1; fi
steps.method_note: Concurrent burst of 6 simultaneous POST /api/missions with identical (templateKey,goal) using test.echo (not research). test.echo is proven with a healthy matching fleet to land ≥1 HTTP 200 ok:true create and multiple 403 bodies with body-level code WIP_ONE_EXCEEDED in the same burst; research previously failed the entire burst with MISSION_RUNTIME_FAILED (fleet/manifest drift), so WIP never appeared in response bodies. Unique idempotency keys and a unique goal timestamp per run; args.goal MUST equal goal. Script prints full R_i response bodies so the JSON fragment "code":"WIP_ONE_EXCEEDED" appears only in body lines (honest body-level proof). Assertion expect_log_regex requires that body fragment and therefore fails on echo-only logs that merely reprint # literal_cmd (no self-matching bare-token grep). Fail path emits NO_WIP_IN_BURST via split shell vars so the contiguous token is not present on the # literal_cmd line; success also prints runtime-assembled STEP2_PROOF=ok+wip_body from split vars.

steps.text: POST verdicts {advance->validated} with no recorded probe - refused; add a probe - accepted.
steps.literal_cmd: echo '=== 3a: unprobed advance against test.echo run 019f8d2d (no research.plan@1) -> expect PROBE_REQUIRED_FOR_VALIDATED ==='; A=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/api/missions/019f8d2d-2ef7-711b-bb40-df20ab9f27e4/verdicts -H 'Authorization: Bearer rn-gate-s23' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"verdict":"advance","targetStatus":"validated","rationale":"Advance before any probe.","requestKey":"gate-step3a-unprobed-advance"}'); echo "$A"; echo '=== 3b: probed advance against run 019f8d2e (committed research.plan@1, rn-authorized) -> expect accepted ok:true ==='; B=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/api/missions/019f8d2e-00db-7eda-8ef3-51ee6cd81018/verdicts -H 'Authorization: Bearer rn-gate-s23' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"verdict":"advance","targetStatus":"validated","rationale":"Advance after a committed research.plan@1 probe.","requestKey":"gate-step3b-probed-advance"}'); echo "$B"; echo; if echo "$A" | grep -q 'PROBE_REQUIRED_FOR_VALIDATED' && echo "$B" | grep -q '"ok":true'; then echo 'STEP3_VERDICT=refused_then_accepted'; else echo 'STEP3_VERDICT=other'; fi
steps.method_note: 3a posts advance->validated to a run with NO committed research.plan@1 probe (test.echo run 019f8d2d) -> trigger refuses with PROBE_REQUIRED_FOR_VALIDATED. 3b posts the same to run 019f8d2e which HAS a committed research.plan@1 stage_run (and is rn-scope authorized) -> trigger allows, handler accepts. Summary token is computed from the two real responses.

steps.text: POST /api/missions/:id/steer mid-run - the steering row takes effect on the following cycle without a restart.
steps.literal_cmd: curl -sS -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4111/api/missions/019f8d2e-00db-7eda-8ef3-51ee6cd81018/steer -H 'Authorization: Bearer rn-gate-s23' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"instruction":"Prioritize recent papers published in 2025 and 2026.","requestKey":"gate-step4-steer"}'
steps.method_note: expect_log_regex '"eventType":"steer"' is unique to a successful steer response (the event row is only written on success). The embedded run object may carry a prior retrieve-error code that is irrelevant to steer success, so no expect_not_log_regex.

steps.text: Run holo mission:cycle <id> - the CHALLENGE instance differs from ASSAY; refuting claims pass the identical admission gate.
Run holo fulcrum:authorable-check - a fulcrum template compiles against contract+ledger+gate+role-bindings+publish seams with zero new platform code.
